name: Volcanoes National Park
description: Rwanda's most famous park, home to mountain gorillas and golden monkeys across the Virunga chain. Treks depart early from Kinigi headquarters.
localTip: Gorilla permits sell out months ahead — book before you fix your dates, not after.

name: Lake Kivu
description: One of Africa's great lakes, with beach towns at Gisenyi, Kibuye and Rusizi. Swimming is safe: there are no crocodiles or hippos.
localTip: Kibuye is quieter than Gisenyi and the island boat trips leave from there.

name: Kigali Genocide Memorial
description: The memorial at Gisozi where more than 250,000 victims are buried. Permanent exhibitions cover the 1994 genocide against the Tutsi and its aftermath.
localTip: Allow a full two hours and plan nothing demanding afterwards. Entry is free; the audio guide is worth it.

name: Nyungwe National Park
description: Ancient montane rainforest with chimpanzee tracking and East Africa's only canopy walkway, suspended 50 metres above the forest floor.
localTip: Chimp tracking starts at 5am. Stay inside the park the night before or you will not make it.

name: Kimironko Market
description: Kigali's largest market: produce, spices, kitenge fabric and tailors who will make a garment in a day.
localTip: Saturday morning is the market at full tilt. A Wednesday afternoon is a different, much quieter place.

name: Inema Arts Center
description: Artist-run studio and gallery in Kacyiru showing contemporary Rwandan painting and sculpture, with resident artists working on site.
localTip: Thursday evenings there is live music and the studios stay open late.

name: Akagera National Park
description: Rwanda's savannah park in the east, with lion, rhino, elephant and buffalo restored over the past decade. Boat safaris run on Lake Ihema.
localTip: The southern gate is a two and a half hour drive from Kigali — leave before dawn for a same-day visit.

name: King's Palace Museum
description: Reconstruction of the traditional royal residence at Nyanza, including the long-horned Inyambo cattle and their praise singers.
localTip: The Inyambo cattle ceremony happens on request — ask at the gate when you arrive, not later.

name: Musanze Caves
description: A two-kilometre lava tube formed by the Virunga eruptions, with bat colonies and openings to the surface.
localTip: Wear closed shoes. The floor is loose volcanic rock and it stays wet year round.

name: Ethnographic Museum
description: Rwanda's richest collection of ethnographic and archaeological material, housed in Huye in a building gifted by Belgium in 1989.
localTip: Combine it with the National Art Gallery at Rwesero — they are twenty minutes apart.

name: Heaven Restaurant
description: Terrace restaurant in Kiyovu serving Rwandan and pan-African dishes, with a view over the city and a well-known cocktail list.
localTip: Book a table before sunset for the view. Walk-ins after 7pm rarely get the terrace.

name: Mount Bisoke
description: Day hike up a 3,711-metre volcano to a crater lake at the summit, inside Volcanoes National Park.
localTip: Six hours round trip and the descent is pure mud. Hire gaiters and a walking stick at the base.
